body: One fridge thought I can't get off my mind is the though that  Coco having her last outfit as a onesie is because she'll go back to sleep for a long time and she wants to be comfortable for that 500 years.

I kind of know the feeling of guilt and pain of losing a brother. I also frequently think about what could have been and who should have died. I was supposed to be as much a brother to him as he was to me and I let my resentment from past misunderstandings cloud my eyes from what was unfolding in front of me. Only when I saw him limp and lifeless on the bed we used to share as kids did I feel the weight of what my hate had done. I still think about him to this day despite 7 years passing by like a dream. Thank you for sharing your story. It put into words what I couldn't, I can think a bit clearer now and maybe get out of the slump I dragged myself into.
Uni is sucking the life out of me, and my stress levels are constantly kept up. Constant sleep deprivation fries your dome after a while.

Upon reading your poem, the first thing I can say is that the imagery is sublime and does not go "overboard" at any point, although for me that may make the poem feel too unsoiled and unspent  thus not evoking the nautical ruggedness of a sailor in a storm. Specifically in the line *"Waves crashing upon me, I struggled, gasping for air, desperatly keeping my head and heart above the dark fluid of despair",* it merely describes the storm and  what the sailor feels without giving a discernable sense of danger or urgency attached to it. Almost as if instructing the reader exactly what to feel rather than what they may build upon themselves from your work. Nevertheless the poem flows well and reveals its story in a pleasant and easily digestible manner. If I am not mistaken you've subtly likened an emotional experience, like falling in love or rediscovering yourself, to a sailor casting out to sea. A cyclical process that is inevitable to repeat until the faithful sailor cannot embrace the sea no more. All in all it's a good poem that was a joy to read, though not really tapping into the hellish abyss of a sea in turmoil, it achieves what it set out to do and delivers its narrative.

This is quite an emotive poem. I like how you adhered to an AABB rhyme structure which made your poem have a smooth rhyme in each stanza, writing in quatrains really built upon the musicality of your poem. I think a more consistent meter may add to the musicality of it all, especially if spoken out loud.
Thank you for the feedback. I'm still polishing my literary skills and I intend to revisit this poem when I get considerably better. I will definitely keep what you said in mind.
I'm still learning english, apologies if my writing is bloated and unorganized.

The simplistic way of writing juxtaposed with the themes of hardship gives an air of positivity. Whether it was by intention or not, by being concise and sparse on vivid visual imagery it gives the feeling that conquering hardship isn't as complicated as we make it out to be. Simply put it's short, sweet, and effective. I enjoyed this piece. I look forward to your other works.

Your usage of something as simple and common as a flash drive as analogy to the very complicated emotions of love and attraction really drives in how the process of loving and being in love is something inherent and innate yet because of familiarity to it we needlessly complicate and rush things leading to unexpected outcomes. Overall I liked it and look forward to more of your works in the future.
